- **Supine** → roll the leg **out** (bag under the **other** hip, ≈20°) → cut on the **posteromedial border**

- Between **pes anserinus** and **medial gastrocnemius** → lift popliteus + soleus off the back
- **Prone (Lobenhoffer)** → **medial gastrocnemius** pulled lateral, **semimembranosus** medial → no fossa dissection

7B.07.b:
### Anterior (anteromedial) tibia
- Cut **1–2 cm lateral** to the crest → **never over the bone** (thin skin)
  [[FIG: Fig 7B.36, 7B.37 · 7B.07
- **Long cut, gentle retraction**; plane → **none**
- **Medial face** → plate on the **tension** side, easy to bend; **lateral face** → lift **tibialis anterior** (the only muscle there)
- Dangers → **long saphenous vein + saphenous nerve**; **stripping periosteum** → dead fragments do not unite
- **Anterolateral face** (bad medial skin) → leave the fascia **open**; distal third → **anterior tibial artery + DPN** (deep peroneal nerve) (AO)
- Shaft → **triangular** → 3 borders, 3 surfaces (Hoppenfeld)

### Posterolateral tibia (Harmon)
- When the front skin is bad, nonunion grafting → lateral or **prone**
  [[FIG: Fig 7B.38, 7B.39 · 7B.07
- Plane → **gastrocnemius, soleus, FHL (flexor hallucis longus) (tibial)** / **peronei (superficial peroneal)** → true
- Soleus + FHL off the fibula → across the **interosseous membrane** → back of the tibia
- Dangers → **peroneal artery branches** (tie), small saphenous vein; tibial nerve + artery **safe behind TP (tibialis posterior) and FHL**
- Not into the **proximal quarter** → popliteus + the bundle

### Fibula (Henry)
- Cut **behind the fibula**, up along the **biceps**
  [[FIG: Fig 7B.40, 7B.41 · 7B.07
- Plane → **peronei (SPN)** / **soleus + flexors (tibial)**
- **CPN first** → on the back of the biceps → follow it round the **neck**
- Strip muscles **from below up**; strip the membrane **from above down** (fibres run the other way)
- Dangers → **CPN** at the neck; **SPN** at the middle/distal third junction; peroneal artery near the malleolus

### Tibial nail entry
- **Infrapatellar** → knee **100–120°**, 5-cm cut **beside (or through) the patellar tendon** → knee pain the same either way (AO)
  [[FIG: Fig 7B.42 · 7B.07
- **Entry** → **medial side of the lateral tibial spine** on the AP, **anterior edge** of the plateau on the lateral → **extrasynovial** (AO, Hoppenfeld)
- Errors → **posterior**: ACL + anterior horn medial meniscus; **medial**: **valgus**; **lateral**: varus; **low**: splits the anterior cortex
- **Suprapatellar (semi-extended)** → cut **4 cm above** the patella → through the quadriceps tendon → keep the **sleeve** in (protects the cartilage) (AO)
  [[FIG: Fig 7B.43 · 7B.07
- Dangers → **infrapatellar branch** (numbness), thigh rest in the fossa → popliteal vein

### Two-incision fasciotomy
- **Anterolateral** → over the septum between anterior and lateral → **SPN**
  [[FIG: Fig 7B.44, 7B.45 · 7B.07
- **Medial** → ≈2 cm **behind** the posteromedial border → **saphenous vein + nerve** → lift soleus for the **deep posterior**
- Compartments → 7A 7.12

### Pins and wires — safe zones (AO)
- **Anteromedial face** → safe all along
- Avoid **tibiofibular** wires at the **fibular neck** (CPN)
- Only **1–2 threads** past the far cortex

| Approach | Plane | Nerves |
|---|---|---|

| **Fibula** | Peronei / soleus-flexors | Superficial peroneal / tibial |
| Medial gastrocnemius / semimembranosus | Both tibial → **safe**, not true | — |

HIGH YIELD
- Round the knee → **no true plane** in most approaches → safe because the nerves are **behind**
- The true planes are on the **lateral side** → ITB / biceps, vastus lateralis / biceps, and in the leg **peronei vs the back muscles**
